terms.es: El infinitivo después de los verbos

en.title: The infinitive after verbs
en.summary: Many English verbs are followed by the to-infinitive.

paragraphs: The infinitive is the base form of the verb, usually used with to: to go, to speak, to be. After many verbs, English uses the to-infinitive to show a wish, a plan, a decision or an attempt.

blocks.html:
GroupVerbsExample
wishes and planswant, hope, plan, intend, expectI hope to travel.
decisionsdecide, choose, agree, refuseHe refused to pay.
attemptstry, manage, fail, learnShe managed to win.
promisespromise, offer, threatenHe promised to call.
seem and appearseem, appear, happenIt seems to work.

paragraphs: Some verbs take an object before the infinitive: someone is told, wanted or allowed to do something.

blocks.html:
VerbExample
ask, tell, orderShe told him to wait.
want, would like, expectI want you to come.
allow, let, permitThey allowed us to leave.
advise, remind, warnHe advised me to rest.

paragraphs: After modal verbs, and after make and let with an object, the base form is used without to: I can swim; She made him wait; Let me go.
The to-infinitive can answer the question Why?: I went to the shop to buy bread. For a negative purpose, use in order not to: He spoke quietly in order not to wake the baby.

items: Wrong: **I want that you come.** Right: **I want you to come.**
Wrong: **She made me to wait.** Right: **She made me wait.**
Wrong: **I can to swim.** Right: **I can swim.**
Wrong: **I went to shop for to buy bread.** Right: **to buy bread**
